Explanation: Files the agent changed, with lines added and removed and edits; and its test runs.
Source: agent_detail files and tests.

Explanation: One error key: every time it happened, with agent and message.
Source: board_api.error_detail (GET /api/board/error).

Explanation: Raw hook and OpenTelemetry events of the session with kind, tool and stored detail. Newest 500.
Source: GET /api/events and /api/events/count.

Explanation: Tool failures and API errors of the agent, with time and message, and the newest loop.
Source: agent_detail errors and loop.

Explanation: Lines around a given line of a context file, for the places a finding or a skill read points to.
Source: board_api.file_excerpt (GET /api/board/excerpt), limited to discovered tool files.

Explanation: One file: its edits over time, the last two stored versions for a diff, and the sessions that wrote it.
Source: board_api.file_detail (GET /api/board/file) over file_write_events and file_history.

Explanation: Each event with time, type, model, input and output tokens, cache read, duration and first token.
Source: board_api._session_flow: store rows (requests, tool_invocations, session_prompts, context_events) merged with hook and OTel events.

Explanation: Turns, tool calls, subagents, hooks, errors, compactions, total tokens, largest turn and time to first token of the session.
Source: board_api._flow_summary over the merged flow events.

Explanation: Individual API call records received via OpenTelemetry — model, latency, tokens, errors. Provides per-request visibility.
Source: Aggregated from OTel receiver events matching gen_ai.* span types. Each call logged with model, duration_ms, input/output tokens, status, and optional error details.

Explanation: VS Code language-model tokens by extension: tokens in and out, calls, models.
Source: board_api._lm_by_extension over analysis.lm_usage.

Explanation: Rate-limit windows the tool reported for the session: used share and reset time.
Source: board_api._rate_limit: newest events row whose detail holds rate_limits.

Explanation: MCP servers: calls, errors, total time and last call, and servers configured but not used.
Source: GET /api/session-mcp-usage over tool_invocations of MCP tools.

Explanation: Compactions: time, trigger, tokens before and after, duration.
Source: context_events rows of kind compaction.

Explanation: Context size per call (first, last, peak), tool definitions, tools available, and the split at shutdown (system, conversation, tools).
Source: board_api._agent_context over requests.max_prompt_tokens, tool_tokens, available_tools and context_events.

Explanation: Branch, commit and dirty state of the project at the session.
Source: board_api._agent_git, with commits from /api/session-commits.

Explanation: CPU, RAM and network of the agent's process tree, and tokens a minute.
Source: board_api._agent_resources from the collector snapshot and process_snapshots.

Explanation: Earlier runs in the same project with duration, tokens and file churn against the median of the others.
Source: board_api._agent_runs over the sessions table.

Explanation: Skills the agent used, with uses and who started them.
Source: board_api._agent_skills over skill_uses.

Explanation: Messages, tokens, cached share, cost, tool calls with failures, time and lines for one agent.
Source: board_api.agent_detail: the agent row plus file_write_events lines.

Explanation: Live process tree of the session and the recorded process list kept after it ends, with role, CPU, RAM and the programs started.
Source: agent_detail resources.process_tree and GET /api/session-processes.

Explanation: One prompt: full text, prompt file, and the input, output, cache read, duration and tool calls of its turn.
Source: board_api.prompt_detail (GET /api/board/prompt).

Explanation: One skill: who can see it, uses, agents, trigger and file reads.
Source: board_api.skill_detail (GET /api/board/skill).

Explanation: Subagents and tasks the tool reported: state, model, task, time and tokens. States: active, idle, ended, not started; tasks: pending, active, done.
Source: GET /api/session-stats (entity state built from hook events and subagent files).

Explanation: Model calls and tool calls on one time line: time, input and output, cache, duration, prompt, error, agent, target, result.
Source: board_api._store_flow_events rows shown by TimelineTab.

Explanation: Tool calls of the agent: time, name, target, duration, result. Newest 200.
Source: agent_detail tool_calls from tool_invocations.

Explanation: One tool name: every call with time, agent, duration, target, result and confirmation.
Source: board_api.tool_detail (GET /api/board/tool).

Explanation: Each turn: prompt, reply, model calls, tool calls, tokens and duration. Text is shown only when the tool keeps it.
Source: board_api.agent_transcript: turns built from session_prompts, requests and tool_invocations, merged with hook turns.

Explanation: Turns oldest first with prompt, tokens, time and tools.
Source: agent_detail turns over session_prompts and requests.

Explanation: Calls per time slot, as a small trend.
Source: _activity_for: request and tool-call counts per spark slot.

Explanation: Cache read as a share of all input tokens.
Source: cache_read_tokens / (input + cache_read + cache_creation) of the agent.

Explanation: Confirmations the agent asked for.
Source: COUNT of tool_invocations rows with a confirm value.

Explanation: Cost of the agent at stored cost or list price.
Source: SUM(requests.cost_usd), else _list_cost from the model price table.

Explanation: CPU of the agent's live processes.
Source: Sum of cpu_pct of the session's pids in the collector snapshot; falls back to the live session figure.

Explanation: Time from the first record to the last, or to now while it runs.
Source: started_at and ended_at of the session or subagent, else the first and last record timestamps.

Explanation: Failed tool calls of the agent.
Source: COUNT of those rows with is_error set.

Explanation: Input tokens without cache.
Source: SUM(requests.input_tokens) of the agent.

Explanation: RAM of the agent's live processes.
Source: Sum of mem_mb of the session's pids in the collector snapshot.

Explanation: Models the agent called.
Source: Distinct requests.model values of the agent.

Explanation: User, assistant and tool messages of the agent.
Source: _agent_row msgs: session_prompts (user), requests (assistant), tool_invocations (tool).

Explanation: Output tokens.
Source: SUM(requests.output_tokens) of the agent.

Explanation: Project folder of the agent.
Source: sessions.project_path, else requests.project_path.

Explanation: Run state of the agent: running, looping, waiting, idle, ended or stopped.
Source: board.status for main agents and board.sub_status for subagents, from live processes, the newest request and its finish_reason.

Explanation: The AI tool the agent runs in.
Source: sessions.tool, else requests.tool of the session.

Explanation: Tool calls of the agent.
Source: COUNT of tool_invocations rows of the agent that are not permission records.

Explanation: Runs, messages, tokens, cost and tool failure rate per kind of agent (main agents, then subagents by task).
Source: compute_board by_role: agents grouped by agents.task, main agents first.

Explanation: An agent that is looping, or waiting for you to confirm a tool call, with the detail, cost so far and since when.
Source: board_api._attention: loops that are at the end of the session with status looping, and agents with status waiting and a pending confirmation.

Explanation: Sessions that are alive or recent but whose turn has ended and nothing runs.
Source: compute_board kpis.idle: sessions in scope with status idle (turn ended, last activity within IDLE_AFTER_S or process alive).

Explanation: Agents running now: sessions in view whose status is running, looping or waiting.
Source: compute_board kpis.running: count of sessions in scope whose status is in ACTIVE_STATUSES. Status comes from live processes, the newest request and the finish reason.

Explanation: Subagents that are running, looping or waiting.
Source: compute_board kpis.subagents_running: agents other than the main agent of each session in scope, with an active sub status.

Explanation: One row per model: agents, calls, tokens, input, output, cache read, cache write, cached share, cost and p95 reply time.
Source: compute_board by_model: requests grouped by model; p95 is the 0.95 percentile of duration_ms of that model. Cache write is null for tools that never report it.

Explanation: Per file: lines added and removed, edits, agents and last edit.
Source: board_api._changes_section over file_write_events.detail lines_added and lines_removed.

Explanation: A memory or instruction file with the tool that reads it, scope, tokens per call, lines changed in the range, who changed it and when.
Source: board_api._memory_files: files with category memory or instruction, joined to file_write_events.

Explanation: Passing test runs whose output is piped to a filter, which can hide a failure.
Source: compute_board tests_piped: passing runs whose target matches _PIPED_TO_FILTER_RE without pipefail.

Explanation: Per test command: runs, failed, median duration, state now (passing, failing, flaky) and last run. A test is a tool call whose target contains test, jest or tox.
Source: board_api._tests_section over tool_invocations; failure is is_error or a non-zero exit_code.

Explanation: Activity status of a memory file — green (live active, recently changed), orange (modified within 5 minutes), grey (inactive).
Source: Based on file mtime comparison: green if changed since last collection, orange if mtime within 300s, grey otherwise.

Explanation: Estimated token count for a single memory/context file.
Source: ceil(len(content.encode('utf-8')) / 4). The content is read from disk on each collection cycle.

Explanation: Time series chart showing growth of agent memory tokens over time. Tracks how much persistent context AI tools accumulate.
Source: board_api._context_growth: mem_tokens and memory_entries of system_snapshots, at most 120 points over the last 7 days, each the last value of its time slot.

Explanation: Total estimated tokens across all agent memory/context files. These are persistent memory entries that AI tools load into their context window (e.g. Claude's CLAUDE.md, user memory files, Copilot instructions).
Source: Memory files are discovered by scanning known paths (e.g. ~/.claude/memory/, ~/.claude/projects/*/memory/). Each file's content is token-estimated via ceil(utf8_bytes / 4). Summed across all entries.

Explanation: Number of discovered files that the tool never sends to the model.
Source: tools.compute_token_budget never_sent_count.

Explanation: Per project: always, on-demand and conditional tokens, and the estimate with the global files as a share of the window.
Source: board_api._context_budget projects[]: (global_tokens + project tokens) / window.

Explanation: Tokens of the always-loaded files that stay after a compaction.
Source: tools.compute_token_budget survives_compaction_tokens.

Explanation: Model context window used for the share figures: the known size of the detected model, else 200 000 tokens (marked assumed).
Source: board_api._context_budget: model_pricing.context_window_for(model), else DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW.

Explanation: Tokens from files always loaded into the context window on every LLM call. This is the guaranteed baseline context consumption.
Source: compute_token_budget() classifies files: sent_to_llm="yes" AND loaded_when="every-call". Sums token estimates for matching files. Includes global scope + largest sub-project.

Explanation: Tokens from files marked as cacheable — can be served from prompt cache, reducing cost and latency.
Source: Files where cacheable="yes" in paths-*.csv. These files benefit from prompt caching when the AI provider supports it.

Explanation: Tokens from files loaded conditionally based on project type or feature flags.
Source: Files where sent_to_llm in ("conditional", "partial"). Summed token estimates.

Explanation: Tokens from files loaded on-demand. Not always in context but available when referenced.
Source: Files where sent_to_llm="on-demand" OR loaded_when="on-demand". Summed token estimates.

Explanation: Current context window usage as percentage of detected model's maximum context length. Color-coded: green <50%, yellow <80%, orange >=80%.
Source: (always_loaded_tokens / model_max_context) * 100. Model max context detected from tool telemetry model field. For max potential: sums all projects (not just largest).

Explanation: The AI model detected for context window size estimation. Used to calculate what percentage of the model's context window is consumed.
Source: From tool telemetry model field or tool config model setting. Determines max context length for percentage calculation.

Explanation: Estimated context window usage for the largest sub-project, plus global tokens. Shows realistic total when multiple projects exist.
Source: compute_token_budget() groups files by project root, finds the largest sub-project by token sum, adds global (non-project) tokens. Fields: largest_project name, largest_project_tokens, global_tokens.

Explanation: Largest files by name per project and kind, with the rest folded into (other).
Source: board_api._context_map items: top CONTEXT_MAP_ITEMS file names per (project, kind).

Explanation: Token distribution broken down by project. Shows how context budget is split across different working directories/repositories.
Source: Files grouped by resolved project root (git root or parent directory). Each project's tokens = sum of file estimates within that project scope.

Explanation: Tokens from files loaded conditionally (e.g. only in certain project types or when specific features are enabled).
Source: Files where sent_to_llm in ("conditional", "partial") in paths-*.csv. Token count estimated per file, summed.

Explanation: Tokens from files that exist on disk but are never sent to the LLM. Configuration, state, and metadata files that the tool uses internally.
Source: Files where sent_to_llm="no" in paths-*.csv. Token count estimated per file, summed.

Explanation: Tokens from files loaded on-demand (only when referenced or needed). These don't consume context by default but contribute when activated.
Source: Files where sent_to_llm="on-demand" OR loaded_when="on-demand" in paths-*.csv. Token count estimated per file, summed.

Explanation: Tokens from files that are always sent to the LLM on every call. These consume context window capacity on every interaction and represent the baseline context load.
Source: Files where sent_to_llm="yes" AND loaded_when="every-call" in paths-*.csv. Token count estimated per file, summed.

Explanation: Calls, input, output, cache read, cache write, total tokens and cost per local day and model, for the last 7 days.
Source: board_api._context_daily over requests, grouped by local date and model.

Explanation: Calls, tokens and cost per local day and model for the last 7 days, as a stacked chart and a table.
Source: board_api._context_daily over the requests table, grouped by local date and model. Cost is the stored cost, else the list price.

Explanation: File content for the preview of a context file in the board. Returns raw text of tracked files.
Source: GET /api/file: direct file read, limited to 200 KB. The path must be in the allowed set (discovered tool files).

Explanation: Each context file with tool, kind, scope, size, tokens, whether it is sent to the model, when it loads and whether it changed in the last 5 minutes.
Source: board_api._context_file over the collector's discovered files. Tokens are ceil(bytes / 4).

Explanation: File activity indicator — green pulse (actively changing), orange (recently modified), grey (inactive).
Source: Based on file mtime: green if changed since last collection cycle, orange if mtime within 300s, grey otherwise. Pulsing animation for live- active files.

Explanation: Whether this file is sent to the LLM and under what conditions. Diamond = always, diamond-outline = on-demand, circle = conditional/no.
Source: sent_to_llm field from paths-*.csv for this file's path pattern. Values: "yes", "on-demand", "conditional", "partial", "no".

Explanation: File size in bytes from the filesystem.
Source: os.stat(path).st_size.

Explanation: Estimated token count for a single file.
Source: ceil(len(content.encode('utf-8')) / 4).

Explanation: Total number of configuration, instruction, and context files discovered across all monitored AI tools on disk. Counts files matching known path patterns from paths-unix.csv (or paths-windows.csv on Windows).
Source: File discovery expands path templates from paths-*.csv using tool- specific root strategies (home dir, XDG config, project root). Each expanded path is checked for existence via os.stat(). The count is sum(len(tool.files)) across all tools, excluding aictl's own files.

Explanation: Total estimated tokens across all discovered AI tool files. Represents the cumulative context footprint — how many tokens the LLM ecosystem consumes on disk for instructions, memory, rules, and configuration.
Source: Each file's token count is estimated as ceil(utf8_byte_length / 4), approximating BPE tokenization. Summed across all files for all tools. Formula: sum(ceil(len(content.encode('utf-8')) / 4)) for each file.

Explanation: When a cached lifetime source was last computed, and the cost quality (reported, estimated or unknown).
Source: board_api._context_telemetry as_of and cost_quality. A cost of 0 with no price source shows as unknown, not free.

Explanation: Per-model tokens, requests and cost inside a tool's own lifetime totals.
Source: board_api._context_telemetry by_model, from the tool's own statistics file.

Explanation: The newest 20 errors a tool logged, with type, message and model.
Source: board_api._context_telemetry errors, newest first.

Explanation: Total API duration in milliseconds across all sessions. Used to detect timeout patterns (avg > 30s flags potential issue).
Source: Accumulated from session.shutdown events in Copilot CLI events.jsonl. Field: totalApiDurationMs. If avg per request > 30000ms, flagged as timeout error.

Explanation: Lifetime cache-read tokens — tokens retrieved from prompt cache instead of re-processing. Reduces cost and latency.
Source: From tool stats: costTracker.totalCacheReadTokens (Claude Code), modelMetrics.*.usage.cacheReadTokens (Copilot), etc.

Explanation: Lifetime cache-creation tokens — tokens written to prompt cache for future reuse. Initial investment for cache read savings.
Source: From tool stats: costTracker.totalCacheCreationTokens (Claude Code), cacheWriteTokens (Copilot), cached_input_tokens (Codex), etc.

Explanation: Estimated total cost in USD across all sessions for this tool. Based on the tool's own cost tracking, not recalculated by aictl.
Source: From tool stats: costTracker.totalCostUSD (Claude Code), modelMetrics.*.requests.cost (Copilot), usage.cost_usd (Codex). Passed through from tool's native calculation.

Explanation: Errors encountered while collecting telemetry for this tool. Includes parse errors, missing files, permission issues, and API timeouts.
Source: Accumulated during telemetry parsing. Each parser catches exceptions and records error type + message. Copilot-specific: timeout detection if avg API latency > 30s/request.

Explanation: Lifetime input tokens consumed by this tool — total tokens sent to the LLM across all sessions. Verified from the tool's native stats.
Source: Tool-specific parser reads the tool's stats/telemetry file: - Claude Code: ~/.claude/stats-cache.json → costTracker.totalInputTokens - Copilot CLI: events.jsonl → session.shutdown → modelMetrics.*.usage.inputTokens - Codex CLI: session.json → usage.input_tokens - Cursor: state.vscdb SQLite → keys matching %token% - Continue: sessions/*.json → usage.promptTokens

Explanation: Total number of messages (user+assistant turns) across all sessions.
Source: From tool stats: costTracker.totalMessages (Claude Code). Not all tools expose message counts.

Explanation: Lifetime output tokens generated by this tool — total tokens received from the LLM across all sessions.
Source: Same tool-specific parsers as input_tokens, reading the output counterpart field from each tool's native stats format.

Explanation: Number of premium API requests used (Copilot CLI). Tracks quota consumption for rate-limited plans.
Source: Accumulated from session.shutdown events in Copilot CLI events.jsonl. Field: totalPremiumRequests. Summed across all shutdown events.

Explanation: Total number of sessions recorded by this tool's telemetry.
Source: From tool stats: costTracker.totalSessions (Claude Code), count of session.shutdown events (Copilot), count of session files (Codex).

Explanation: Tokens per tool and file kind (instructions, rules, memory, skills and so on), with the part sent to the model and the part never sent.
Source: board_api._context_categories: the tool's discovered files grouped by kind; the sent part follows the budget bucket of each file.

Explanation: Tokens of each tool's context files in total, sent to the model and never sent.
Source: board_api._context_categories tokens, sent and never_sent per tool.

Explanation: Number of files in a specific category (instructions, config, rules, memory, state, etc.) for a tool.
Source: Files grouped by category field from paths-*.csv. Count per category per tool.

Explanation: Total tokens for all files in a category for a tool.
Source: Sum of per-file token estimates within the category.

Explanation: Token distribution broken down by file category (instructions, config, rules, memory, state, etc.). Shows which category of files contributes most to context window usage.
Source: Files grouped by their 'category' field from paths-*.csv. Token count per category = sum of per-file estimates within the category.

Explanation: Number of CPU cores, to read the per-core bars.
Source: compute_machine cpu_cores from the collector snapshot.

Explanation: Time series of CPU utilization for a specific tool over the selected time range.
Source: Historical tool_metrics.cpu values from DB, queried for the selected tool and time range.

Explanation: Total CPU utilization across all monitored AI tool processes, expressed as a percentage where 100% = one full CPU core. A value of 400% means four cores are fully utilized by AI tools.
Source: psutil.Process.cpu_percent() is called for each monitored process on every collection cycle (default 1.0s interval). Values are summed across all processes belonging to AI tools. Live correlator data is preferred; falls back to per-process discovery data if unavailable.

Explanation: Per-core CPU utilization for every logical CPU core on the system. Displayed as color-coded bars (red >80%, orange >50%, green >20%). Shows overall system load, not just AI tool processes.
Source: psutil.cpu_percent(interval=0.1, percpu=True) returns a list of percentages, one per logical core. Called on every snapshot render.

Explanation: Count of headless browser processes (Chrome, Chromium, Firefox) spawned by AI tools. These are resource-heavy and may indicate tool-use loops or web scraping.
Source: Process matching against browser process name patterns in the process tree of AI tool sessions.

Explanation: Count of MCP server processes whose parent process has died. These orphans consume resources but are no longer useful.
Source: MCP server processes where the expected parent AI tool process is no longer running (ppid check fails or parent PID not in active session PIDs).

Explanation: Total count of process-level anomalies across all AI tools. Aggregates memory leaks, CPU spikes, zombie processes, and other unusual behavior.
Source: Sum of anomaly counts from all tool process inspections. Each anomaly type has its own detection rule (see procs.tool.anomaly).

Explanation: Alert triggered when total memory consumption by AI tool subagent processes exceeds 2GB. Indicates potential memory leak or runaway agent.
Source: Sum of psutil.Process.memory_info().rss for all processes classified as subagents or child processes. Threshold: 2 * 1024^3 bytes.

Explanation: File events the monitor saw for the tool.
Source: board_api._monitor_section per_tool.file_events from live.file_events.

Explanation: How sure the token estimate is, and from which source.
Source: per_tool.est_confidence and est_source from live.token_estimate.

Explanation: Size of the tool's workspace folders.
Source: board_api._monitor_section per_tool.workspace_bytes from live.workspace_size_mb.

Explanation: Inbound network rate of a tool, in bytes per second, from the In column of the Network, tokens and files panel.
Source: Live monitor _recent_rate() over the recent_network deque; board_api._monitor_section per_tool.inbound_bps.

Explanation: Outbound network rate of a tool, in bytes per second, from the Out column of the Network, tokens and files panel.
Source: Live monitor _recent_rate() over the recent_network deque; board_api._monitor_section per_tool.outbound_bps.

Explanation: Current CPU utilization and peak CPU seen during this tool's active sessions.
Source: Sum of cpu_percent across sessions (current). Max of peak_cpu_percent across sessions (peak). From SessionCorrelator aggregation.

Explanation: Number of unique files touched (created/modified/deleted) during this tool's active sessions.
Source: Set union of files_touched across all sessions for this tool. File events detected by filesystem watching or state dir scanning.

Explanation: Whether MCP (Model Context Protocol) loop activity is detected for this tool, and estimated number of tool-use loops.
Source: Heuristic MCP loop detection analyzing 24-sample windows: - Network bursts >32KB → min(0.45, count * 0.15) - CPU spikes >20% → min(0.30, count * 0.10) - Subprocess invocations (git, rg, bash) → min(0.35, count * 0.08) - Correlation bonus +0.15 if CPU AND network active Detected if combined score >= 0.45. Loop count estimate = max(0, network_peaks // 2).

Explanation: Number of OS process IDs attributed to this tool's active sessions.
Source: Union of all pids across SessionState objects for this tool.

Explanation: Number of active sessions for this specific tool.
Source: Count of SessionState objects for this tool where last_seen is within 180s. From SessionCorrelator tool aggregation.

Explanation: Estimated tokens for this tool's active sessions, with confidence level indicating estimation method used.
Source: Tiered estimation: exact telemetry (0.95) > session file inference (0.60) > network inference (0.40). Source and confidence displayed alongside the value.

Explanation: Working directories (project roots) associated with this tool's active sessions.
Source: Set union of session.workspaces, derived from the cwd of root processes. Resolved to git repository roots when possible.

Explanation: The command that ends a process, offered as a copy action.
Source: board_api._cleanup_of builds a kill command for the pids of an alert or row.

Explanation: Process name, PID, owning tool and the agent it belongs to.
Source: board_api.machine_processes over snapshot.tools[].processes and live- monitor pids.

Explanation: The process that started this one.
Source: process record ppid.

Explanation: Number of running OS processes attributed to AI tools. Includes IDE extensions, language servers, daemon processes, and CLI instances. Uses the higher of discovery count vs live PID count per tool.
Source: Process discovery uses psutil.process_iter() and matches each process against ps_grep_pattern regexes from processes-*.csv. The count per tool is max(len(discovered_processes), live_pid_count_from_correlator). Summed across all tools.

Explanation: Process anomaly detection — unusual resource consumption, unexpected state, or known problematic patterns.
Source: Anomaly rules applied per process: memory exceeding known thresholds (memory_active_mb from CSV), CPU spikes, known leak patterns (known_leak + leak_pattern from CSV), orphan detection.

Explanation: CPU utilization for a single process, as percentage of one core. Color- coded: orange >5%, red if anomaly detected.
Source: psutil.Process.cpu_percent(None) / 100 for the specific PID. Updated on each collection cycle.

Explanation: Resident memory (RSS) of a single process, in the RAM column of the Processes panel.
Source: psutil.Process.memory_info().rss in bytes, carried as mem_mb in the snapshot.

Explanation: Classification of each process — app, helper, mcp-server, cli, subagent, language-server, daemon, etc.
Source: Direct read from processes-*.csv process_type column, matched to the running process via ps_grep_pattern regex.

Explanation: Risk level that this process may become a zombie (orphaned, not properly cleaned up). Based on known patterns from processes-*.csv.
Source: Static classification from processes-*.csv zombie_risk column (none, low, medium, high). Based on historical analysis of each process type's lifecycle behavior.

Explanation: Time series of memory usage for a specific tool over the selected time range.
Source: Historical tool_metrics.mem_mb values from DB, queried for the selected tool and time range.

Explanation: Total resident memory (RSS) consumed by all monitored AI tool processes, in megabytes. Shows physical RAM footprint of the AI tool ecosystem.
Source: psutil.Process.memory_info().rss is read for each monitored process. Values are summed across all AI tool processes and converted to MB (bytes / 1048576).

Explanation: A prompt file (AGENTS.md style) in a project, its parent folders or the user folders, and how many prompts used it.
Source: board_api._project_prompts: session_prompts.prompt_file grouped by file and project.

Explanation: A user prompt with time, text, project and the tokens of its turn.
Source: board_api._prompts_section: session_prompts rows with agent_id empty. Text is masked for secrets; tokens are the whole turn's tokens.

Explanation: Number of user prompts in the range.
Source: compute_board prompts_total.

Explanation: A skill with scope, agents that used it, uses and the tokens of the turns where it ran.
Source: board_api._skills_section: skill_uses rows; turn tokens come from _turns.

Explanation: Workflow and prompt files of the tools with their type, size, tokens and last change.
Source: board_api._context_workflows over the collector's file inventory: files whose path or kind marks a workflow or prompt.

Explanation: A setting of a tool: key, value in force, scope, file and line, risk flag and whether it is documented.
Source: GET /api/settings/tools: orchestrator.full_tool_configs(), the complete settings records including defaults no file sets.

Explanation: IDE extensions installed for this tool (e.g. VS Code extensions related to the AI tool).
Source: Enumeration of ~/.vscode/extensions directories matching known patterns for the tool. Also from VS Code extensions list.

Explanation: Every file aictl reads for the settings view: stat facts, git state and how many settings read it.
Source: api_handlers.settings_files over tool configs, audit sources and monitored folders. No file is opened.

Explanation: Whether aictl's hooks are installed for a tool.
Source: GET /api/hooks-status, shown by HookStatus.js.

Explanation: MCP servers configured in this tool's settings. Lists server names as pills.
Source: Parsed from tool MCP config (e.g. Claude Code's ~/.claude/settings.json mcpServers, or project .mcp.json files).

Explanation: The model in force per tool and agent, with conflicts and pins.
Source: GET /api/effective-models.

Explanation: The AI model currently configured for this tool (e.g. claude- sonnet-4-5-20250514, gpt-4o). Extracted from the tool's settings file.
Source: Parsed from tool config files defined in tool-configs.yaml. For Claude Code: settings.json → selectedModel. For Cursor: state.vscdb SQLite. For Copilot: settings.json model preferences.

Explanation: Feature flags and settings extracted from the tool's configuration. They show which capabilities are enabled or disabled.
Source: Parsed from tool config files per the feature extraction rules of tool- configs.yaml. Boolean and string values.

Explanation: Actionable suggestions generated from analyzing the tool's current configuration. Warnings about suboptimal settings, missing features, or security concerns.
Source: Generated by _generate_hints() in tool_config.py based on OTel config state, feature flags, and tool settings analysis.

Explanation: Allow, ask and deny rules per tool, derived from the permission settings.
Source: settings/permissions.js derivePermissions over the same tool_configs rows.

Explanation: Whether OpenTelemetry export is enabled for this tool, and the configured exporter type and endpoint.
Source: Parsed from tool config files. Looks for OTel-related settings (exporter, endpoint, protocol) in the tool's configuration.

Explanation: Whether OpenTelemetry is configured to capture message content (prompts and responses). Warning shown if enabled due to privacy.
Source: From tool OTel config: captureContent or capture_content field in VS Code settings or tool-specific config files.

Explanation: Whether automatic updates are enabled for the tool.
Source: Claude Code: ~/.claude.json autoUpdates field. Other tools: from respective settings files per tool-configs.yaml.

Explanation: Whether the tool is configured to launch automatically at system startup (login items on macOS, autostart on Linux).
Source: macOS: detected via osascript querying login items or launchd plist. Linux: checks XDG autostart directory. Windows: checks startup folder.

Explanation: A finding of the hidden-context audit: severity, rule, tool, file and line, what it does.
Source: context_audit scan served by /api/context-audit, shown through findings.js.

Explanation: The value in force of each setting per tool, taken from tool_configs.
Source: snapshot.tool_configs entries, ranked by scope (managed, project-local, project, user).

Explanation: A failure with tool, message, kind (tool or API), count, agents and last time. Numbers in messages are folded to #.
Source: board_api._errors_section: tool_invocations with is_error (result_summary) and requests with error_type or http_status.

Explanation: Model reply time: count, p50, p95, p99 and max.
Source: board_api._latency over requests.duration_ms > 0.

Explanation: Agent run: time from start to end of each agent.
Source: compute_board latency_rows: ended_at - started_at of agent rows.

Explanation: Tool call duration: count, p50, p95, p99 and max.
Source: board_api._tools_section durations of tool_invocations.duration_ms > 0.

Explanation: Time to first token. Shown as not reported for tools that never send it.
Source: board_api._latency over requests.ttft_ms > 0.

Explanation: Whole turn: time from a prompt to the last reply or tool result before the next prompt.
Source: board_api._turns: session_prompts timestamps joined to requests end times.

Explanation: A loop: agent, status, the repeated pattern, repeats, tokens and cost spent in it, and since when.
Source: board_api.find_loops over tool_invocations of each session; tokens and cost are summed from requests in the loop's time range.

Explanation: Failed tool calls as a share of all tool calls.
Source: compute_board kpis.fail_rate: failures / tool_calls.

Explanation: Failed tool calls in the range. API errors are in the Failures panel.
Source: compute_board kpis.failures: tool_invocations with is_error set. Null when no tool in view reports tool calls.

Explanation: Agents repeating the same failing work.
Source: compute_board kpis.loops: count of visible loops found by find_loops over the tool calls of each session.

Explanation: 95th percentile of model reply time (p50 shown with it).
Source: compute_board kpis.p95_ms and p50_ms: percentiles of requests.duration_ms > 0.

Explanation: Tool calls in the range, including totals that a tool reports without rows.
Source: compute_board kpis.tool_calls: tool_invocations rows that are not permission records, plus the fallback totals of session_usage.

Explanation: Per tool name: calls, failed, failure rate, p50, p95 and max duration, and a trend.
Source: board_api._tools_section over tool_invocations; durations only from rows with duration_ms > 0.

Explanation: Per tool: calls run automatically, approved, denied, blocked by a rule, and the median wait for an answer.
Source: board_api._confirms_section over tool_invocations.confirm and confirm_wait_ms.

Explanation: What cache reads saved against the full input price.
Source: compute_board saved_usd: cache-read tokens times the difference between input and cache-read list price of each model.

Explanation: Cache read share of input per time bucket.
Source: compute_board series.cached_share.

Explanation: AI credits GitHub Copilot reports for the sessions in view. A credit is the tool's unit, not dollars.
Source: board_api._credits_section: HistoryDB.query_session_usage daily billing_amount for sessions active in the window; days cut by a window edge count whole.

Explanation: Cost per time bucket, split by tool, project or model.
Source: compute_board series.cost.by_tool, by_project, by_model.

Explanation: Tokens whose model has no known price, so they carry no cost.
Source: board_api._unpriced_section: tokens of models for which no stored cost and no list price exists, with their share of all tokens.

Explanation: User, assistant and tool messages per time bucket.
Source: compute_board series.messages: session_prompts, requests and tool_invocations per bucket.

Explanation: Agents in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: Sessions and their subagents with this project_path.

Explanation: Failed model calls in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: requests with is_error set.

Explanation: Cached share in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: cache_read / all input tokens of the project.

Explanation: Cost in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: SUM(cost_usd) or list price of requests in the project.

Explanation: Lines added and removed in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: SUM of lines_added and lines_removed in file_write_events.detail.

Explanation: Loops in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: Visible loops by project of the session.

Explanation: Messages in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: Model calls plus prompts plus tool calls of the project.

Explanation: 95th percentile reply time in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: requests.duration_ms > 0, grouped by project.

Explanation: User prompts in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: COUNT of session_prompts rows with agent_id empty.

Explanation: Test runs and passed test runs in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: _tests_section: tool_invocations whose target looks like a test command.

Explanation: Tokens in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: SUM of token columns of requests with this project_path.

Explanation: Tool calls in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: tool_invocations of the project's sessions.

Explanation: Share of tool calls that failed in the project.
Source: compute_board projects: failures / tool calls of the project's sessions.

Explanation: Share of input served from the prompt cache.
Source: compute_board kpis.cached_share: cache_read / (input + cache_read + cache_write).

Explanation: Cost of the range at the stored cost per call, or at list price when the call has none. Not a bill.
Source: compute_board kpis.cost_usd: requests.cost_usd where stored, else _list_cost from the model price table.

Explanation: User, assistant and tool messages in the range.
Source: compute_board kpis.messages: model calls plus prompts plus tool calls, including the totals a tool reports without rows.

Explanation: The same totals over the window before this one, for the change shown under each tile.
Source: board_api._previous: the filters re-applied to [since - span, since); null when that window holds no data.

Explanation: Input, output, cache read and cache write tokens of all model calls in the range.
Source: compute_board kpis.tokens: sum over the usage cube built from requests, plus sessions that only have a session_usage total.

Explanation: Tokens per time bucket, split into cache read, input, cache write and output.
Source: compute_board series.tokens: usage cube buckets of requests.

Explanation: Name of each data collector in the monitoring pipeline (e.g. process, network, discovery, filesystem, telemetry).
Source: Keys from SessionCorrelator.diagnostics() dict. Each collector reports its status via on_collector_status(source, status, mode).

Explanation: Operating mode of each collector (e.g. polling, watching, passive).
Source: Direct assignment from the mode parameter in SessionCorrelator.on_collector_status().

Explanation: Current status of each collector — active, degraded, disabled, or unknown.
Source: Direct assignment from the status parameter in SessionCorrelator.on_collector_status(). Updated on each collector cycle.

Explanation: Workspace and state directory paths being monitored by the live collector.
Source: Workspace roots from active session working directories. State paths from tool-specific state directory functions (e.g. claude_global_dir(), copilot_state_dir()).

Explanation: API errors a tool logged, from its telemetry record.
Source: board_api._freshness errors = len(telemetry.errors).

Explanation: Per tool: where its data comes from (requests, session usage), the newest record, freshness of the live monitor and API errors.
Source: board_api._sources over _source_rows: MAX(ts) of requests and MAX(last_activity_at) of session_usage per tool and source; freshness from _freshness.

Explanation: Confidence score (0-100%) for the telemetry data accuracy. Higher confidence means the data comes from a more reliable source.
Source: Set by each parser: - 0.95 (95%): Direct tool stats (Claude stats-cache, OTel spans) - 0.90 (90%): Copilot events.jsonl shutdown events - 0.85 (85%): Codex session.json - 0.75 (75%): Continue session files - 0.70 (70%): Cursor SQLite state - 0.60 (60%): Session file inference - 0.40 (40%): Network traffic inference

Explanation: An ingester: status (ok, off, no source, waiting or failing), last OK, last read, rows on the last read and in all.
Source: board_api._ingester_rows from ingester_runner.collect_status and data_quality.

Explanation: A data-quality event: time, severity, component, status, message and how often it was seen.
Source: board_api._quality_rows over db.query_data_quality (last 50).

Explanation: Per data kind and tool: exact, partial, estimate, needs hooks or not reported.
Source: board_api.coverage_rows: what the store holds per tool (_store_facts) against the static expectations of each tool.

Explanation: CPU and RAM of aictl's helper processes next to the daemon.
Source: board_api._self_usage children.

Explanation: History store size live and on disk, the limit, the bytes that compaction can free, and the retention days.
Source: board_api._self_section: db.storage_status() and db._retention_days.

Explanation: Samples emitted, written, dropped and buffered by the sample sink, and whether flood protection is on.
Source: board_api._sink_section from sink.stats().

Explanation: Browser windows on the live stream, and the age of the newest snapshot.
Source: compute_machine pipeline.stream: connected clients and now - snapshot.timestamp.

Explanation: Whether the OTel receiver has received data in the last 300 s. The aictl itself panel shows Active, or No data for 5 min, under Metrics in.
Source: Derived: time.time() - OtelStats.last_receive_at < 300.

Explanation: Total API calls detected across all OTLP sources (metrics, logs, traces). Includes both log-based and span-based API call detection.
Source: OtelStats.api_calls_total counter. Incremented when event name matches API_REQUEST_EVENTS set or span name matches API patterns.

Explanation: Total API errors detected across all OTLP sources. Includes log-based errors and span status code 2 (ERROR).
Source: OtelStats.api_errors_total counter. Incremented when event name matches API_ERROR_EVENTS set or span has error status.

Explanation: Total count of event/log records received across all /v1/logs and /v1/traces POST requests since server startup.
Source: OtelStats.events_received counter. Incremented by len(events) after each parse_logs() or parse_traces() call.

Explanation: Timestamp of the last successfully parsed OTLP payload from any endpoint. Used to determine receiver freshness.
Source: OtelStats.last_receive_at set to time.time() after any successful parse. Active if within 300s. Displayed as relative time.

Explanation: Total count of metric data points received across all /v1/metrics and /v1/traces POST requests since server startup.
Source: OtelStats.metrics_received counter. Incremented by len(samples) after each parse_metrics() or parse_traces() call.

Explanation: Number of errors encountered while parsing incoming OTLP payloads across all three endpoints (metrics, logs, traces).
Source: OtelStats.errors counter. Incremented on JSON parse failures, schema validation errors, or unhandled exceptions in any receiver handler.

Explanation: CPU use of the aictl service process itself. This is not an AI tool metric: it is the cost of the monitoring.
Source: board_api._self_usage: psutil cpu_percent of the aictl process plus its helper processes. Also served by /api/self-status.

Explanation: Total number of rows across the main data tables in the aictl database (metrics + tool_metrics + events + samples).
Source: SUM of SELECT COUNT(*) from metrics, tool_metrics, events, samples tables.

Explanation: On-disk size of the aictl SQLite history database (history.db). Grows as metrics, events, and telemetry are collected over time. Compacted automatically (24h full res, 7d 1-min avg, 30d 5-min avg).
Source: os.stat(db_path).st_size for the history.db file. Default location: ~/.config/aictl/history.db.

Explanation: Resident memory (RSS) consumed by the aictl monitoring service. This is the physical RAM footprint of aictl itself, not the monitored AI tools.
Source: psutil.Process(os.getpid()).memory_info().rss in bytes.

Explanation: Number of threads in the aictl monitoring service. Includes DB flush thread, refresh loop, SSE connections, collectors.
Source: psutil.Process(os.getpid()).num_threads().

Explanation: How long the aictl monitoring service has been running since the last start of 'aictl daemon serve'.
Source: time.time() - psutil.Process(os.getpid()).create_time().
